title: S3-Tracker: Self-Supervised Surgical Tissue Tracking With Contrastive Random Walks
abstract: arXiv:2609.14313v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Robust point tracking in endoscopic videos is essential for computer-assisted intervention and autonomous robotic surgery, enabling continuous registration between intraoperative video and preoperative imaging despite soft tissue deformation. However, supervised tracking methods depend on large annotated datasets, while surgical conditions make reliable trajectory annotation challenging. We propose a self-supervised Track-Any-Point approach that learns from unlabeled surgical videos by establishing global pixel correspondences and inferring point trajectories through contrastive random walks. Trained without annotations, our method achieves performance comparable to existing semi-supervised approaches while implicitly handling tissue deformation. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of self-supervised point tracking in surgical environments and its potential to reduce reliance on annotated data.

translated_title: S3-Tracker：基于对比随机游走的自监督手术组织跟踪
translated_abstract: 在内镜视频中进行鲁棒的点跟踪对于计算机辅助干预和自主机器人手术至关重要，它能够在软组织变形的情况下实现术中视频与术前影像之间的连续配准。然而，有监督的跟踪方法依赖于大规模标注数据集，而手术条件使得可靠的轨迹标注极具挑战性。我们提出了一种自监督的任意点跟踪方法，通过建立全局像素对应关系，并利用对比随机游走推断点的轨迹，从而从无标注的手术视频中学习。我们的方法无需任何标注进行训练，即可达到与现有半监督方法相当的性能，同时能够隐式地处理组织变形。这些发现证明了在手术环境中进行自监督点跟踪的可行性，及其减少对标注数据依赖的潜力。
tldr: 提出了无需标注的自监督任意点跟踪方法S3-Tracker，通过对比随机游走从无标注手术视频中学习点轨迹，性能可与现有半监督方法媲美，并可隐式处理组织变形。
en_tdlr: We propose S3-Tracker, an annotation-free self-supervised Track-Any-Point method that learns point trajectories from unlabeled surgical videos via contrastive random walks, achieving performance comparable to semi-supervised approaches while implicitly handling tissue deformation.
